name: TrapWrap
subcategory: AI rap and music video generation
tagline: Turns a prompt into an AI rap track with a matching captioned video.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The pipeline is not mysterious: write lyrics with an LLM, render a vocal, lay it over a beat, force-align the words, burn animated captions onto a looping visual, export vertical. An agent can assemble that end to end with ffmpeg and a few API calls in a weekend, and the output will be recognizably the same shape of thing. What you cannot build is the part that makes rap sound like rap: flow, timing, pocket, and a voice that does not sound like a podcast narrator reading bars. That piece comes from hosted music models you rent either way, so the DIY version is a wrapper around someone else's wrapper. Build it if you want control over the template and the caption style, not if you want the vocals to land.
coreLoopDIY: A local script that takes a topic, writes lyrics, generates a vocal over a chosen beat, word-aligns it, and burns karaoke captions onto a vertical video.
requirements: API key for a text model (lyrics)
API key for a music or voice generation model
a small library of licensed instrumental beats you actually have rights to
local whisper or a hosted transcription endpoint for word-level timing
whatYouLose: Vocal quality: rented models still rarely nail flow and pocket, and yours will not be tuned for it
Preset visual templates and transitions that already look like a music video instead of a slideshow
Beat library with clear licensing, which is a legal problem and not a code problem
Phone-friendly capture, preview, and one-tap export to TikTok or Reels
Someone else absorbing model cost spikes and API deprecations
moatNotes: The music generation layer is rented by everyone, including the app, so the real differentiation is template taste and beat licensing.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the difference between a rap video and a text-to-speech slideshow is about forty small aesthetic decisions, and an app that has already made them is worth more than a script you have to babysit. Add the beat licensing question, which a personal build usually answers by ignoring it, and paying a few dollars to get a sharable vertical clip in ninety seconds is a reasonable trade for anyone who wants the output more than the process.
notes: The pipeline is a weekend; the flow is not.
prompt:
Build a local command line tool called barwrap that turns a topic into a vertical rap video. No accounts, no web app, no telemetry.

Stack: Python 3.11, click for the CLI, ffmpeg for all audio and video work (shell out, do not wrap a library), faster-whisper for word level timing. Secrets in .env, loaded with python-dotenv. Dependencies in requirements.txt.

Pipeline, in this order:
1. Lyrics: call an OpenAI chat model with the topic, a target bar count, and a style note. Output 16 bars max, plain text, one bar per line. Save to out/lyrics.txt and print it.
2. Pause for approval: show the lyrics and ask to continue, regenerate, or edit in $EDITOR.
3. Vocal: call ElevenLabs text to speech with the approved lyrics and a voice id from .env. Save out/vocal.mp3. Document clearly in the README that this gives spoken bars, not rapped bars, and that swapping in a music generation API is the upgrade path. Keep the vocal step behind a single function so it can be replaced.
4. Beat: read an instrumental from beats/ chosen by filename flag. Ship no audio in the repo, just a beats/README.md explaining the user must supply files they have rights to.
5. Mix: ffmpeg amix the vocal over the beat, duck the beat by 6dB under the vocal using sidechaincompress, normalize with loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
6. Timing: run faster-whisper on the vocal only to get word level timestamps.
7. Captions: generate an ASS subtitle file with one or two words on screen at a time, large centered bold text, a karaoke style highlight on the active word.
8. Video: take a still image or looping clip from assets/, scale and crop to 1080x1920, loop to match audio length, add a slow zoom, burn in the ASS subtitles, mux the mixed audio, export out/video.mp4 as h264 + aac.

In scope: one command, barwrap make --topic "..." --beat trap1.mp3 --bg loop.mp4, that runs the whole chain with progress printed per step and intermediate files kept in out/ so steps can be rerun.

Out of scope: a GUI, uploading anywhere, multiple caption themes, voice cloning, beat generation, mobile anything.

Write a README with setup steps, required .env keys, an honest paragraph on where the output falls short of a real rap video, and a note on beat licensing.
